summary: State-sliced CSVs of US physical therapists and PT clinics extracted from the CMS NPPES weekly public download. The full national dataset contains 337,000+ licensed PTs across all 50 states; each record includes practice name, individual PT name, NPI number, address, phone, specialty taxonomy (physical therapist, PT assistant, occupational therapist, speech-language pathologist), and credential type. USADoctorList.com charges for the same NPPES-derived PT database; OpenMart charges for verified PT clinic owner contacts; no low-cost one-time state CSV is available on the market. A state-sliced file at $29–$39 targets PT EMR software SDRs, rehab equipment suppliers, staffing agencies, and healthcare insurance brokers who need a current list of active clinics in a specific state without paying for a national healthcare database subscription.

audience.who: PT/OT EMR and practice management software vendors (WebPT, SPRY, TherapyBrands, Clinicient, Raintree) whose SDRs cold-call clinics and outpatient practices; durable medical equipment and rehab supply companies; physical therapy staffing and travel PT agencies; healthcare liability and malpractice insurance brokers; continuing education providers selling PT CEU courses; billing and revenue cycle companies targeting outpatient rehab practices.

data_wanted: Practice/business name, individual PT name, NPI number, address (street, city, state, ZIP), phone number, fax (where available), specialty taxonomy code (e.g., 225100000X = Physical Therapist, 225200000X = Physical Therapy Assistant, 225X00000X = Occupational Therapist, 235Z00000X = Speech-Language Pathologist), credential type, enumeration date — all sourced from the CMS NPPES weekly downloadable file at npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov, no login or API key required.

OpenMart charges for 90K+ verified PT owner contacts. WebPT's SDR team and competing EMR vendors (TherapyBrands, SPRY, Raintree) all maintain outbound motions requiring state-level PT clinic lists. A one-time $29–$39 state CSV is 50%+ cheaper than the nearest NPPES-derived competitor while targeting the same EMR SDR who needs 2,000–8,000 PTs in a specific state for a campaign.
